rv.q: Portraying Toni is a tall order, and Bonner succeeds.
Lydia R. Diamond’s play “Toni Stone,” now running at the Goodman Theatre, provides a compelling character study of a woman driven to achieve what she was told she couldn’t.
Toni Stone is by far one of the best plays in Chicago.
"Toni Stone" is among her best work.
Not only is this an entertaining piece of theatre, it’s also an important piece of theatre.
The result is a mesmerizing, enlightening and thoroughly entertaining evening of theatre that kicks off Black History Month with the crack of a bat.
Full of history, herstory and heart, from the beginning you’ll be root, root, rooting for Toni Stone.
But by the end it still feels like we're retiring Toni's jersey after witnessing a remarkable story.
Even if you are not into baseball, you will find this production a delight to watch.
Toni Stone is an excellent illustration of how history can come to life onstage in all its messy, ugly, and glorious truth.

cn.t: Critics praise Lydia R. Diamond's play for illuminating the forgotten story of baseball's first Black female professional player. The production earns strong reviews for its engaging, non-linear storytelling and heartfelt performances.
